items.title: Louis Tio Interview, 1960-10-26
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now there was another one of your sisters you mentioned before I got the names mixed up. [INTERVIEWEE] Josephine. ... [INTERVIEWEE] No, Alice T. O. Long.

ctx.x: So he told my mother, this is no place for us to raise our children. We got to get out of here. Well, he went to Bay St. Louis. Well, in Bay St. Louis everything was pretty cheap. You had house rent was cheaper. They had work. Then he had his music. He had his people just to send him orchestration to write from all parts of the city and different bands. He made money at it. He told my mother that he was going to write to the Mexican council, which he did. He had written to him and he told him that he wanted to…

When did your father die before I forget? I forgot to ask. About what year? If you don't remember exactly, you know, was it the time of the First World War or before? Must have been before that then. Alice. Oh, Alice. Yeah? Come here a minute please. Sorry to bother everybody. No, that's alright. These things are very interesting to us to do something like that.
Tell me something. How old were you when Papa died? Year and a half.
